messages:
sre_bot: INCIDENT PAGE: high error-rate + request backlog on /v1/generate for hosted-east-1 - paging oncall (priority: P1) :rotating_light:

samir: I have the pager, joining. any customer-facing impact yet? :eyes:

alex_chen: affirmative — some 502/504 returned, spike in 95th latency, and queue depth from the request aggregator shows sustained ~12k pending. we recently saw normal is <500.

maria_gomez: putting brief impact note in ops: several small customers reporting timeouts, one mid-size customer seeing retries. Notified CS to hold new signups.

jordan: logs look like a backlog at the inference queue level; HPA didn't add replicas for the inference service. kube HPA metrics show stable CPU but custom metric (queue_depth) is spiking.

kai_patel: oncall checklist: 1) assess immediate mitigation (fallback model / limit concurrency) 2) check GPU pool utilization 3) evaluate warmup delays for new pods 4) consider scale-up of node pool / burst capacity

alex_chen: quick mitigation: switching routing policy to fallback-model-small for non-SLA customers to shed load. applying route flag now.

alex_chen: /flag rollout: set route=hosted-east-1:default->fallback-small for tag=non-sla

```bash
# pseudo-commands
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/flags \ 
  -d '{"route":"hosted-east-1","target":"fallback-small","filter":"!sla"}'
```

maria_gomez: routing change done. seeing ~30% reduction in queue depth in the dashboard. still have ~8k pending.

jordan: checking k8s: HPA for inference-service-east shows minReplicas=10 maxReplicas=200,targetMetric=queue_depth, currentReplicas=12, currentQueue=8200. HPA controller logs show repeated evaluation errors: "unable to fetch custom metric: timeout" starting ~1803456720.

samir: that would explain why HPA didn't scale. is metrics-server flapping?

kai_patel: I can access metrics API: query to custom-metrics returns 504 occasionally. seeing latency to Prometheus-adapter. Possibly partial outage of metrics pipeline.

ops_shift: GPU pool status: east-pool-1 capacity at 98% allocatable GPUs. Several pods in Pending with reason=ContainerCreating and a few with reason=NodeAffinity/Allocatable. kube-scheduler logs show "insufficient GPUs" for most pending pods.

maria_gomez: so two compounding issues: metrics adapter flaked causing HPA not to scale, and even if HPA triggered, GPU capacity near-saturation preventing new pods from scheduling.

alex_chen: can we spin up burst nodes in the autoscaler? normally we have burst-capacity pool reserved for emergencies. requesting immediate scale to +20 GPUs in burst pool.

jordan: sent scale request to infra autoscaler via API. response: accepted, expected nodes provisioning in ~5-7 minutes. provisioning logs: control-plane started gang scheduling.

samir: in the meanwhile, warmup delays: pods that do get created take ~90-120s to finish model load (weights) and become ready. KV cache is cold, so first requests are heavy. That multiplies queue delays.

kai_patel: suggestion: enable lightweight stub model (tiny) for retries for 180s to let pods warm up. Also reduce concurrency-per-pod to lower head-of-line blocking.

alex_chen: applied temporary policy: set concurrency=1 on inference-service-east for 10 minutes, and enable stub model for non-sla.

```yaml
# applied policy snippet
service: inference-service-east
concurrency: 1
fallback_model: stub-tiny
ttl: 180
```

maria_gomez: after concurrency change, observed more pods becoming healthy but throughput per-pod lower. queue shrank to ~4.6k after 6 minutes.

jordan: autoscaler report: new nodes started, GPU allocatable increased by 24 GPUs at 1803456960. scheduler started placing pending pods. by 1803457000 we have 36 active GPU pods.

samir: careful: even after scheduling, those pods will warmup. expect latency improvements to be gradual over next 3-5 minutes.

ops_shift: monitoring shows model-loading failure on 2 pods: OOM during preload. they crashed looped. logs: "OOMKilled while preallocating model weights". skipping those pods.

kai_patel: OOMs mean our weights prefetch is overcommit on certain instance types. decreasing prefetch buffer on startup for those nodes via config map. patching now.

alex_chen: patched configmap to set PRELOAD_BUFFER=0.6 for gpu-type-a. new pods coming up ok.

maria_gomez: at 1803457020 queue down to ~900 pending. customer retries still causing elevated errors but overall SLA impact limited to a 15-20m window for some customers. CS updated impacted customers.

jordan: root cause hypotheses (collecting):
- H1: metrics-adapter intermittently failing prevented HPA from scaling when queue_depth spiked. (evidence: adapter timeouts ~1803456720 - 1803456880)
- H2: sustained traffic spike exceeded reserved GPU pool capacity resulting in pods Pending due to insufficient GPUs. (evidence: pool at 98% allocatable, many Pending with insufficient GPUs)
- H3: warmup/model preload latency plus OOMs delayed useful capacity coming online (evidence: 90-120s load times, 2 OOM crashes)
- H4: combined head-of-line blocking due to concurrency-per-pod default high (8) amplified queue depth (evidence: faster recovery after concurrency=1)

kai_patel: logging attachment: sharing snippet of HPA controller errors and metrics-adapter timeouts for RCA timeline:

```text
[1803456715] HPA: evaluating inference-service-east -> fetch metrics
[1803456721] metrics-adapter ERROR: timeout fetching custom metric queue_depth for inference-service-east
[1803456730] HPA: evaluation failed, skipping scaling
[1803456802] metrics-adapter INFO: recovered
[1803456880] metrics-adapter ERROR: partial response to /custom.metrics
[1803456958] autoscaler triggered nodegroup-scale-up +24 GPUs
```

samir: timeline summary for postmortem:
- 1803456680: traffic spike detected at ingress (sustained x7 normal)
- 1803456710: queue_depth crosses alert threshold -> incident bot pages
- 1803456720-1803456880: metrics-adapter intermittent timeouts -> HPA misses scale windows
- 1803456740: GPU pool at 95% then 98% by 1803456830 -> pods Pending due to insufficient GPUs
- 1803456760-1803457020: warmup delays; some OOM crashes at 1803456905
- 1803456960: autoscaler provisions burst nodes +24 GPUs
- 1803457020: queue reduced to <1k, mitigation actions in place

maria_gomez: immediate follow-ups already captured: inform infra to investigate metrics-adapter latency root cause (prometheus-adapter or network), review autoscaler thresholds and pre-warm policy for burst capacity, patch image startup to reduce preload OOMs, and add canary for HPA metrics error handling.

alex_chen: short actionable items we will include in the in-incident RCA:
- add circuit-breaker in HPA logic: if custom metric fetch fails, use fallback signal (queue_depth from aggregator) for N seconds
- increase burst node reservation in east region by 20% during business hours
- implement proactive warmup (keep a small pool of warmed pods) for hot models or pre-pull weights during node provisioning
- add alert for metrics-adapter error rate > 5% in 5m

kai_patel: tagging for postmortem: incident_type=autoscale_shortfall, impact=partial_customer_timeout, duration=~32m, mitigations=fallback-routing, concurrency-limit, burst-scale

ops_shift: handoff note for next oncall: our mitigations remain partially enabled: concurrency=1 for 10m TTL (will auto-rollback), fallback routing live for non-sla, and autoscaler scaled nodes up. Keep an eye on metrics-adapter errors and GPU OOMs.

jordan: I'm dropping cluster logs and HPA/controller traces into the incident channel archive. links: https://internal.redwood/logs/1803456789/hpa-logs ; https://internal.redwood/logs/1803456789/metrics-adapter

sre_bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, incident moving to recovery. Please file a postmortem and label with tags.

samir: thanks team. I'll start the RCA doc draft and assign owners for follow-ups.

alex_chen: closing notes: customer-impact window roughly 1803456710 - 1803457042. primary root causes: metrics pipeline flakiness + exhausted GPU pool + warmup/OOM compounding. Will prioritize metrics reliability and pre-warm policies.

maria_gomez: added Postmortem ticket: PM-4581. owners assigned: metrics-adapter (jordan), autoscaler tuning (kai), startup OOM fix (alex).

sre_bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: moving to post-incident review. :white_check_mark:
